Accept.description: What a person accepted with an approval, beyond the permissions (spec §5.3).

AclGrant.description: One allow ACE, inherited by the subtree.

oneOf.description:
Shared by every launch of its kind (the toolchain, a project's folder, a sign-in
store): granted once, kept.
This session's or this call's own: revoked when it ends.

AclTrustee.description:
Whom an ACE names: a SID (a capability's, derived here) or a container by name (its SID
is Windows', [`super::appcontainer::sid`]).

Actor.description:
Who caused an entry: a person, an agent (with its session and the tool call that ran
`fin`), a plugin or the system. `session` is the agent or UI session (`FIN_SESSION`), not
the envelope's process run; `call` is the harness's tool-call id (`FIN_CALL`).

AdapterId.description:
A GPU by numeric ids only (owner decision 7): never a name or driver string. This is the
wire and journal form; binding a session to an adapter (Windows' LUID, plan 6B-1 Task 6)
is `fin-codecs`' own, never serialised, so no per-boot id reaches a report.

oneOf.description: Shown with the plugin; nothing changes.
The plugin is disabled on refresh by any principal (`PLUGIN_REVOKED`).

AgentApproval.description: `agent.approval`: an approval was answered or expired.

AgentInput.description: A CLI agent session (spec §8.1, §8.5, §8.6; plan 7C Decision 6).

harness.description: `claudeCode`, `codex` or `fake`; the built-in agent needs no sandbox (spec §8.9).

libraryRoots.description: The roots of the libraries the project references (read-only).

signInHome.description:
Detection's host sandbox only (plan 7D Decision 19; Claude Code, `host-<ULID>`, `plan`,
no `fin`, not Windows): `<serverData>/providers/claudeCode/home`, **read only** (`auth
status` reads the account's profile there); the store inside it stays read-write.

signInStore.description:
The harness's sign-in store, inside `<serverData>/providers/<harness>/home/` (spec
§8.6): read and written in place (a file, or Claude Code's `store/` directory).

toolchains.description: The base toolchain list plus the harness's own (files and directories, read-only).

AgentSession.description: `agent.session`: a session started, resumed, was interrupted or ended.

AgentToolCall.description:
`agent.toolCall`: the agent called a tool. `callId` is the `FIN_CALL` its `fin` run
carries; `command` names the `fin` command when the tool ran `fin`.

AgentTurn.description:
`agent.turn`: one model call. Content (training only, in the agent-trace store): the
turn's new input messages, the output, and the system prompt and tool definitions, which
are always blobs so identical prompts are stored once.

Align.description: Horizontal alignment of each line inside the layout box.

Anchor.description: The safe-zone edge a caption block is placed against.

Applied.description: The result of applying a transaction to a project.

member.description: The member's path inside the archive.

ArgProblem.description:
One argument that does not match: `path` is a JSON pointer into the arguments, `reason`
the failing keyword (`type`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `enum`, `const`,
`minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `minItems`, `maxItems`), or
`schema` when the schema itself is outside the subset.

ArgsOmitted.description: Why `args` is absent although training is on.

AssetAdd.description:
`asset.add`: what probing found, by kind (plan 4C Task 7). Each kind carries its own
fields and none of the others': `media` a positive `duration` and its `video`/`audio`
streams; `image` and `svg` an `image`; `lottieTemplate` a positive `duration` and `lottie`;
`font` a `font` (with its whole-file SHA-256); `lut` a `lut`.

kind.description: `media` when absent: a sub-project 4B (schema 1) `asset.add` names no kind.

AssetKind.description:
What an asset is: `media` (video and/or audio; every pre-4C asset), `image`, `svg`,
`lottieTemplate` (a dotLottie template with replaceable slots), `font`, or `lut` (a `.cube`
colour lookup table).

AssetMove.description: `asset.move`: puts `asset` in `bin` (at the top when absent).

Attach.description: `attach`: a helper's job, its files only, and its directories.

Attribution.description: How a tool result's txIds were joined to its call (§12.3).

oneOf.description: Anything else; the sample entry's four-character code is in `AudioTrackInfo.fourcc`.

AudioCodecCaps.description:
One audio codec on this machine (none decode or encode before 6C; the rows carry the
guidance, plan 6B-1 Decision 1).

AudioItem.description:
One item's part of the range: it plays `asset` from `sourceFrom` at `speed` over the
timeline span `[from, to)`. `gain` and `pan` cover that span without gaps, in order. An
item of a nested timeline lists the nested items it sounds through in `via`, outermost
first (its `item` and `track` are its own, on the nested timeline).

AudioParams.description:
The item's own audio: gain in dB, pan in −1…1, fades in seconds. A fade's offset
(schema 4) places its window past the item's edge: the fade-in runs over
`[start − fadeInOffset, start − fadeInOffset + fadeIn)`, the fade-out over
`[end + fadeOutOffset − fadeOut, end + fadeOutOffset)`, and only the part inside the item
sounds. A split sets them so each half keeps the original envelope (spec §5.13).

AudioPlan.description: The items sounding in `[from, to)` of one timeline, in track then time order.

padding.description: Samples to drop at the end.

priming.description:
Samples to drop at the start (encoder delay: edit-list media time, `roll`, Opus
pre-skip).

micros.description: From the redeem to the owner's answer (`approved`, `rejected`).

platform.description: The device's platform, once a device redeemed the offer.

route.description: How the device reached the server, once it redeemed.

BackendClass.description:
Who provides a backend (spec §6.1): the export-encoder policy and the capability report key
on it.

oneOf.description: A GPU API (the compositor's), or a backend not in [`MEDIA_BACKENDS`].

BackendEntry.description: A backend and who provides it.

Basis.description:
What decided a purpose (Decision 8): the build default, the environment, or the user's
settings. Ordered weakest first; a stamp with two bases carries the weaker
([`Basis::weaker`]).

Batch.description: The sub-project 6 batch that closes a `laterBatch` gap.

Bin.description: A folder of assets; `parent` nests it.

BinAdd.description: `bin.add`: a bin named `name`, inside `parent` when given.

BinMove.description: `bin.move`: puts `bin` inside `parent` (at the top when absent).

BinRemove.description: `bin.remove`: takes the empty `bin` off the project.

BlobRef.description:
Large content, stored as a blob (Decision 20): its content address, its length and its
media type ([`names::MEDIA_TYPES`]). Allowed only inside a [`super::class::Content`] field
(`x-fin-blob` marks it for the schema checks and [`super::redact::blob_refs`]).

Body.description:
Large or structured content (the agent kinds): inline JSON, or a [`BlobRef`] when
it would not fit an entry (Decision 20).

BranchCreated.description:
The answer of [`Store::create_branch`](crate::Store::create_branch): the new branch and
its `branch` record on the parent. `dry_run`: planned and rolled back, nothing kept (a
retry of a committed create answers with that create, `dry_run` false).

exportedThrough.description: The highest seq in the folder (0: none).

forkSeq.description: The parent's seq it forks at (0 for `main`).

generation.description: Bumped whenever an import takes records out of this branch's history (a rewind).

name.description: Its display name (`main` for `main`; a branch without an index row: its id).

BranchView.description:
A branch as listings show it ([`Store::branches`](crate::Store::branches), `branch.list`):
`display` is the reference that names it (its name, or `<name>#<id>` for an archived
branch or the second holder of a duplicate name); `head` its head seq (its fork seq until
its first record).

Busy.description: The long call a status was answered during (`status()`'s `busy`).

bytes.description: What the cache holds afterwards (above the target only when the rest is pinned).

CacheStatus.description: `media.cache.status` (`fin cache status`): what the cache holds against its cap.

capBytes.description: Eviction keeps `bytes` at or below this (Decision 12).

pinned.description: Entries with at least one pin (never evicted).

CallLimits.description: The limits of this job's calls and results.

messageBytes.description: The largest envelope line, in bytes.

pageBytes.description: The largest page of a paged reply, in bytes before base64.

timeoutS.description: The job's timeout in seconds (a command's own, at most 60).

CapBackend.description: A backend that serves a codec row, by its `fin_media::backend` name.

hw.description: Runs on hardware (a hardware MFT, VideoToolbox's hardware decoder).

CapLevel.description: How a codec direction is served (v2): in hardware, in software, or not at all.

CapSupport.description: How a codec direction is served on this machine (spec §6.2).

CaptionBox.description: A box behind the block. One equal to the default (transparent, no padding) is no box.

CaptionMerge.description: `caption.merge`: `item` takes in `with`, the next caption on its track.

CaptionPlan.description:
A caption's words at the plan's time, and its layout when it was measured. `layout` is
`null` when it was not, and `unmeasured` says why (plan 4C Decision 36).

words.description: Every word, in order (indices match the layout's word boxes).

CaptionPosition.description:
Where the block sits in its safe zone: against the zone's top, middle or bottom, moved
towards the middle by `offset` (a fraction of the zone's height, 0 to 1).

CaptionSetStyle.description: `caption.setStyle`: `item` takes `style`; `overrides`, when given, replace its overrides.

CaptionSource.description: The transcript artifact a caption came from, and its word range (`[first, end)`).

CaptionSplit.description: `caption.split`: cuts `item` before word `word`; the right part is `id`.

CaptionStyleContribution.description:
A caption style (`fin_core::CaptionStyle` JSON) that `fin style add --from
@pub/pack:<name>` copies into a project.

title.description: A message key in the `en` catalogue for the style's display name.

Capture.description: How faithful a turn's content is (§12.6).

oneOf.description: The request and response bodies as sent and received (the built-in agent).
What a CLI's stream reports.

scripts.description:
The ISO 15924 scripts the entry is offered for (a fallback is chosen by these); each
style's default face covers them.

faces.description: Every face, as `fin_text::font_info` reads it (`warm_cache` checks).

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the whole file: its cache name and its pin.

size.description: Bytes; a download must match it exactly.

variable.description:
A variable font's `wght` axis. Only a variable file may serve several styles (one per
weight in the range; the request's weight drives the axis).

CatalogSource.description:
Where a file can be fetched. A plain source serves the file itself; an archive source
serves an archive (its own `sha256` and `size`) holding the file as `archive.member`.

defaultFace.description: The face a fallback or an entry-level pin uses (a collection holds several).

sources.description: Tried in order: the upstream first, then mirrors serving the same bytes.

Cause.description:
Why an item was relocated: the committed record that last moved or removed `neighbour`,
and its author when the log knows it.

ChromaSiting.description: Where 4:2:0 chroma samples sit relative to luma.

oneOf.description:
Co-sited horizontally with the left luma sample, centred vertically (MPEG-2, H.264
default).
Centred both ways (MPEG-1, JPEG).
Co-sited with the top-left luma sample (BT.2020, AV1 "colocated").

CodecCapabilities.description: What this machine can decode and encode: the shape of `fin-codecs`' `Capabilities`.

CodecCaps.description: One codec (and profile and bit depth, when the row is about one) on this machine.

backends.description: The backends that would serve it, decode first, in the order they are tried.

CodecEntry.description: One codec's support on this machine.

backends.description: The backends that would be used, decode first.

CollectPolicy.description:
A project's collection policy (Decision 13): `finisher.project.json` `collect`, read by
`fin-store` and fed to the journal. `never` binds every collaborator's server: no entry of
the project is recorded, and setting it purges the project's entries. A project whose
policy is not known (not open here) is neither: the journal drops its new entries and
purges nothing.

oneOf.description: Follow each user's privacy settings (the file holds no `collect` key).

CommandContribution.description:
A plugin command (spec §3.8, 8B Task 2), run as `plugin:<id>/<name>` through a
`plugin.command` job.

title.description: A message key in the `en` catalogue.

writes.description: Whether the command returns a transaction (`project.write` for the invoker).

CommandOut.description:
What a command returns, at most one envelope line (1 MiB). `tx` is committed by the host
under the invoker with `baseRev = rev` and `via` set by the host only; plugins propose,
fin-core decides (spec §2.5).

oneOf.description: A transaction of fin-core ops (only from a command whose manifest says `writes`).
Data returned to the caller as is.

CommandOutcome.description: What became of a command run.

oneOf.description: The transaction was committed on the revision the plugin saw.
The branch had moved on: fin-core rebased the transaction and committed it.
fin-core refused it (`CONFLICT`): nothing was committed; `ops` are what was proposed.
The command returned data, or a dry run validated its transaction.

CommandRun.description:
A command run: the host has checked `args` against the command's schema and pinned `rev`
to the head of `branch`. Decoded leniently (a field from a newer host is ignored).

command.description: The command's name in the manifest (not the `plugin:<id>/` registry name).

snapshot.description:
The host's handle on the snapshot it read for this run at submit (opaque to plugins):
every page the run reads comes from that snapshot, of this run only, so a rewind or
rebuild that reaches `rev` again in a newer history is never served from an older one.

CommittedTx.description: A transaction as persisted: with its revision, resolved bindings and diff.

link.description:
The record's kind and links; omitted for an `edit`. Boxed: most txs are edits, and a
link would double the size of every `CommittedTx`.

CompactReport.description:
What one compaction run did (serialised camelCase; `waiting` and `abandoned` as
`[name, why]` pairs).

finished.description: Manifests finished (phase 2) and the segment files deleted.

skipped.description: Why nothing ran (not holding the lease, read-only).

waiting.description: `(manifest or branch, why)`: steps that wait and are retried.

lastRunMs.description: Unix ms of the last run that wrote or deleted something.

pending.description: Manifests seen while holding the lease.

Conflict.description:
One op that cannot be carried to the head: which op of which tx, why (a reason code), the
record to blame when there is one (else null), and what to do. A re-run failure keeps its
error's `details` (an `INVALID_RANGE`'s `min` and `max`, say); other conflicts have none.

details.description: Boxed: rarely present, and it keeps `Result<_, Conflict>` small.

ConsentStamp.description:
The consent an entry was written under (Decisions 12 and 14): the consent revision, the
purposes in force (recorded ∩ current), and the weaker basis of the two purposes.

ConsentState.description: The effective consent as `fin diagnostics show` and `diagnostics.consent` report it.

rev.description: The consent revision: monotonic, persisted in `events/state.json`.

ContainerKind.description: The container family, from `ftyp`'s brands or the EBML `DocType`.

oneOf.description: QuickTime (`qt  ` major brand).
EBML `DocType` `webm`.
EBML `DocType` `matroska`.

ContentLight.description: CTA-861.3 content light level (`clli`), in cd/m².

Contributes.description:
Contributions by kind (spec §4.2): the kinds this host consumes. Validation refuses any
other key as `PLUGIN_CONTRIBUTION_UNSUPPORTED`.

ContributionKind.description: Every key of spec §4.2, consumed or not.

CopyPath.description:
How frames travel between the decoder, the compositor and the encoder (spec §5.4): through
host memory (`copy`; all of 6A) or as shared GPU surfaces (`zeroCopy`, 6G).

CoreError.description: A structured, machine-readable error. `code` is a stable `SCREAMING_SNAKE` string.

CostBasis.description: Where a turn's cost comes from.

oneOf.description: The provider reported what it charged (OpenRouter's usage accounting).
Priced from the catalogue.
A plan sign-in: notional, not charged.

Crop.description: Fractions of the item's size cut from each side.

Ctx.description:
What an entry is about: the project, branch and transaction it joins the op log on, the
author (keyed-hashed: `FIN_AUTHOR` is free text) and the actor.

DefaultValue.description:
A spec's default, as its value would be written (`null`: none, the value is per entity or
the parameter is optional).

DeleteMode.description: How a delete leaves its range: `ripple` closes the gap, `lift` leaves it.

DeviceRule.description: A device node a profile may open (spec §8.10 GPU rows).

blobs.description: Blobs on disk and their bytes (they count against `maxMiB` too).

dropped.description: Entries dropped since the journal opened.

oldest.description: The oldest entry's `ts` and the newest's (ms since the epoch).

projects.description: Every project this server was told about, with its flag now.

skippedUnknownProject.description:
Entries not written since the journal opened because their project's flag was not
known (not open here): not drops, but a sign a caller forgot to open a project.

Diff.description:
What a transaction changed, op by op: each entry names the op that recorded it (`op`),
and both lists are in op order. An op may record any number of changes and shifts.

DirDone.description:
Closes one listing of `dir` (Decision 25): every entry of that listing precedes it in the
job's batches. `complete: false` (an error, a timeout, a placeholder or automount
directory, a nested mount unmounted or replaced) marks nothing missing; `code` says why.
`entries` counts the listing's entries. `volume`: the volume measured at `dir` when it is a
nested mount root (Decision 17, per directory), which the indexer keeps as
[`KnownDir::volume`].

Dirs.description: The job directory and the process's private temp directory.

DisplaySize.description: A picture's display size in px (`VideoInfo.display`).

compatibility.description: The base layer's signal compatibility id (8.1 HDR10, 8.4 HLG, …).

Edge.description: Which edge of an item a trim moves.

Effect.description: One effect of an item (`fx<n>`, addressed as `(item, effect)`); `params` is sparse.

EffectAdd.description: `effect.add`: an effect of `kind` on `item` at index `at` (appended when absent).

EffectPlan.description:
One enabled effect with its parameters resolved at the plan's time. `params` holds the
effect's stored and keyframed parameters (the registry's defaults fill the rest).

EncoderCaps.description: An encoder that encoded the capability probe's test clip (plan 6B-1 Decision 19).

hw.description:
Runs on hardware (VideoToolbox, a hardware MFT, Microsoft's own hardware MFT); the
`hwenc` pool and the proxy kind's resources key on it (Tasks 9, 14).

intraFps.description: Intra-only frames per second at 540p, measured on the test clip (Decision 8).

intraOnly.description: Can encode every frame as a keyframe.

sessionLimit.description: Concurrent sessions that opened, up to 4; absent when not counted.

oneOf.description: A record imported from the folder.
The status changed: [`ProjectStatusView`] (without `busy`).

An import took `branch`'s revs from `from_rev` on out of its history: `quarantined`
records were set aside (`own`: some were this server's) and the branch is at
`generation` of database `incarnation` now.

The database was rebuilt: a new `incarnation`, and every rev read before may hold
something else now.
A background tick, backup or compaction failed (`fatal`: the engine is gone).

The first event after registration when the buffer overflowed: `dropped` events
were lost.
The project file's `collect` flag changed (`default` or `never`).

EntryEncoder.description:
The encoder that made an entry (proxies), for diagnostics and the export rule that a
`gpu`-encoded file never leaves the cache.

EntryFile.description: One payload file of an entry.

blake3.description: BLAKE3 of the file, 64 lower-case hex digits.

EntryMeta.description:
An entry's `meta.json` (spec §7.2): the key and its input, the files and, for proxies, the
original's `MediaInfo`.

media.description: The original's `MediaInfo` (proxies: rotation and pixel aspect are applied from it).

toneMapped.description: How an HDR source was brought to SDR (proxies, plan 6B-1 Decision 9); absent for SDR.

EntryStatus.description: What a merge does with a source record (the review's `status`).

oneOf.description: Copied by the merge.
The target holds its origin root already (merged, picked, or its own).
Its origin root is dropped for the target (`DROPPED`).

Left out, not a conflict: `UNDOES_TARGET_RECORDS`, or `NOT_INCLUDED` by the merge's
limits (`reason` says which).
A conflict: it depends on a record the merge does not copy (`DEPENDS_ON_SKIPPED`).
A conflict of another reason (`reason`, `blame`).

EntryType.description:
The type of a directory entry as listed (never by following a link). Windows reparse
points with a name-surrogate tag (symlinks, junctions, mount points) are `symlink` in a
[`ScanEntry`] (see [`crate::listing`]); anything that is neither a regular file, a
directory nor a link (sockets, devices, FIFOs) is `other`.

Envelope.description:
One journal entry (Decision 2), as read from disk: `payload` is a `Value` (whose schema
is [`AnyPayload`]'s). In memory a payload is an [`AnyPayload`], and the journal's writer
thread serialises an [`EnvelopeRef`], which has the same JSON.

ts.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC.

ErrorInternal.description: An `INTERNAL` error, or one of the store's unexpected codes, returned through `fin-node`.

details.description: The keys of the error's `details` (`DETAIL_KEYS`), never their values.

ErrorPanic.description:
A panic or an uncaught error. Under diagnostics, metadata only: the repo-relative
location (or none, with `thirdParty`), the keyed hash of the scrubbed message (so the same
crash groups without its text) and the thread. The scrubbed message itself is content.
No backtrace frames.

ExcludeSpec.description: The library's patterns, as stored and as sent to a scan worker.

caseSensitive.description: The root's case sensitivity: keys and patterns are folded when `false`.

ExitReason.description: Why a process ended. A closed list (`worker_exit_reasons_closed`).

Expect.description:
What an open must find (Decision 19 step 3): the catalogued size, mtime and, when the
catalog has one, file id. TS `ExpectWire`.

dev.description:
The catalogued entry's device (`ScanEntry.dev`). Nested mounts are catalogued, so the
opener crosses them and checks the opened handle against this device; without one,
the handle must be on the root's mount.

ExportPage.description:
One page of `diagnostics.export`, oldest first. `next` is an opaque position: pass it as
the next request's `cursor`; absent on the last page. `redacted`: content fields (and the
blob references inside them) were removed, as for a caller that is not a person (5A
Decision 22); absent otherwise.

FileGrant.description: One mapped file (or directory, `name` ending in `/`) of the job directory.

bytes.description: The size 5C created it at; absent for a file written by `prepare` and for directories.

FileMode.description: How a mapped file may be used.

FileState.description: A catalog file's state in this server (Decision 34).

oneOf.description: Not cached and not queued: never requested, or background fetching is off.

Filter.description: Which entries to read. Empty fields match everything.

limit.description: Only the newest `limit` matches (still oldest first).

project.description: Entries whose `ctx.project` is this id (in any case).

since.description: Entries with `ts` ≥ this (ms since the epoch).

oneOf.description: Linux: the loopback agent listener `tcp:127.0.0.1:<port>` (spec §8.3).
macOS: `<server-data>/run/fin.sock` (sp5 §4.11).
Windows: the named pipe, reached through its DACL; nothing in the policy.

fallback.description: Entry ids, in the order a text's uncovered scripts look for a fallback.

FontCatalogContribution.description:
A font catalog file (`fin_fonts::FontCatalog` JSON) whose entries join the server's
catalog by entry id (8A Decision 22).

FontFace.description: One face of a font file, as `fin_text::font_info` reads it.

scripts.description: ISO 15924 script codes the face covers.

FontFailed.description: A pinned font file whose fetch failed, retried after `retry_at` (unix ms).

FontFetching.description: A pinned font file being fetched (queued: `bytes` 0): `bytes` of `total` so far.

FontFile.description: An imported font file (plan 4C Decision 37): its whole-file SHA-256, size, format and faces.

FontFileRef.description: A project font asset's file and the SHA-256 its asset pins.

FontFileStatus.description:
One font file. `entry` and `style` name its catalog style, when the catalog lists it;
`keys` are the font keys (`<family>|<weight>|<normal|italic>`) open projects pin it as.

FontMissing.description:
A pinned font file not available: `key` (the face key), its `sha256` and why (`offline`,
`notInCatalog`, `notFetched`, `damaged`, `hashMismatch`, or an asset file's problem).

FontPin.description: One face of one exact file: `face` is the index inside a collection (0 for a single font).

scripts.description: ISO 15924 script codes the face covers (as `fin_text::font_info` reports them).

sha256.description: The whole file's SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex digits.

FontPinOp.description: `font.pin`: pins `key` to `pin`, at `fallback` in the fallback order if given.

FontSource.description:
Where a pinned file comes from: a catalog entry's style (at the catalog version that
pinned it), or an imported font asset.

fallbackOnly.description: Internal: drop only the key's fallback place.

Fonts.description:
The pins, keyed by [`font_key`], and the fallback order (pin keys, first tried first).
Empty until a caption edit pins a face; omitted from the project JSON while empty.

FontsPlan.description:
`fonts.plan`: the `font.pin` ops a client prepends to its tx, and notes about faces or
scripts the catalog cannot pin (`FONT_NOT_IN_CATALOG`), which never fail the plan.

FontsStatus.description:
`fonts.status`: every catalog file's state in this server, then the files pinned by open
projects that the catalog does not list (font assets, files of another catalog).

autoFetch.description: Background fetching is on (`fonts.autoFetch`, and `FIN_FONTS_OFFLINE` unset).

damaged.description:
The font cache or the catalog could not be used (`FONTS_DAMAGED`): nothing is
fetched, and only font assets measure.

FontsSummary.description:
A project's font summary (fin-node, 4C Decision 34): the pinned files missing on this
server, being fetched, and whose fetch failed.

FramePlan.description: The layers of one timeline at `t`, bottom first.

layers.description:
Bottom first: tracks in compositing order, items in time order within a track (a
transition's outgoing item before its incoming one).

textEngine.description:
The text engine (`TextMeasurer::fingerprint`) that produced the plan's caption layouts;
absent when no caption was measured.

oneOf.description:
The caller's plugin data directory (spec §5.1): `<server-data>/plugins/data/<id>/<projectId|_>/`
for uniform `person`/`system` rights, else `plugins/authdata/<id>/<projectId|_>/<authorityKey>/`.
`workspace` is not in v1.

GainSegment.description:
Gain over `[from, to)` in dB: `db` are the end values of the keyframe span the segment
lies in, `u` the segment's progress range through that span, so the dB at progress `x` of
the segment is `lerp(db[0], db[1], ease(lerp(u[0], u[1], x)))` with `ease` from `interp`
(`hold`: `db[0]` throughout). The `shapes` multiply the amplitude.

Generation.description:

ItemLink.description:
`item.link`: makes `items` (at least two, on one timeline, none linked yet) one link group
named `id` (a `$name` placeholder). Internal applies (inverses) may name a literal id: a new
group (the inverse of `item.unlink`, one member included), or an existing one the items
join (the undo of a removal that left a member alone, 4C Tasks 9–10 review).

ItemMove.description:
`item.move`: moves `item` to `track` at `at` (a position in the frame before the op, plan
4C Decision 15), and every member of its link group by the same time on its own track
(only the named item changes track). `ripple` closes the gap it leaves and opens room at
the target on each track; `overwrite` lifts it and carves the target range.

ItemRestore.description:
`item.restore` (internal): puts `item` back on `track` at its `start`. Its id may be a
`$placeholder` (spec §4.3): the item then gets a newly allocated id.

ItemSlide.description:
`item.slide`: moves `item` (alone) by `delta` seconds on its track, trimming the
neighbour touching each side so nothing else moves: the one before it at its end, the one
after it at its start. A side with no touching neighbour needs room in the gap
(`SLIDE_BLOCKED`).

ItemSlip.description:
`item.slip`: moves the source of `item` (a clip or nested item) under it by `delta`
source seconds (`sourceIn += delta`); its place on the timeline and its item-relative times
stay. The source range is policy.

ItemSplit.description:
`item.split`: cuts `item` at `offset` (item-relative seconds, strictly inside it). The left
part keeps the id and ends at `offset`; the right part is a copy (effects keep their ids,
item-relative times move by `−offset`, no link group) named by `id`, a `$name` placeholder.

ItemTrim.description: `item.trim`: moves one edge of `item` by `delta` seconds (positive moves it later).

alone.description:
Internal (every trim's inverse): this item alone, not its link group (plan 4C
Decision 19). A `strict` trim is always alone.

ItemUnlink.description:

leave it).

job's `in/dirs.ndjson` is `{dir, mtimeNs, listed}` (written by the indexer; `listed`
becomes `listed_gen` of the scan's generation) with these fields optional

- `mtime_ns`: the mtime its last listing recorded (`DirDone.mtime_ns`); a poll re-lists the

- `entries`: how many entries that listing held: a listing that drops from N > 0 to 0 is

- `mount_root`: it was the root of a nested mount; when it no longer is, its subtree is

  volume there now (a different key its file ids and sample do not confirm,
  [`crate::volume::same_volume`]) is `ROOT_VOLUME_CHANGED`, also never listed and never
  missing.

LineBox.description:
One line. `x` is the left edge of its ink box after alignment and `width` the box's width,
`top` its top; `baseline` is measured from the layout's top. `words` is the half-open range
of word indices on it.

An ink box is the horizontal union of the line's (or word's) glyph outlines where they are
drawn: glyphs are placed by their advances, letter spacing and shaping offsets, and each
outline's extent (side bearings, overhangs and positioned marks included) is what counts,
so a box may start before the pen or end past the last advance. A glyph with no outline
(a bitmap or colour emoji) counts its advance; whitespace counts nothing.

The project the look is of. Only the host reads it (the kind's `dedupe` and `prepare`);
the worker works from the job directory.

rev.description:
The branch's rev the submitter saw: part of the job's identity (`dedupe`). `prepare`
snapshots the head it finds, and `in/snapshot.json` says which rev that was.

size.description:
The frame size; the timeline's resolution when absent. Each side 1 to
[`LOOK_MAX_SIDE`].

skipped.description: Every frame's, in `at` order, bottom layer first within a frame.

LookStats.description: What a warm worker reused (spec §3.2 item 1: caches keyed by content).

deviceReused.description: The GPU device and pipelines were made by an earlier job of this worker.

sourcesOpened.description: Sources opened (container parsed, decoder made) by this job.

sourcesReused.description: Sources an earlier job of this worker had open.

workerJobs.description: Jobs this worker ran, this one included.

LottieInfo.description: A dotLottie template: its canvas, timing, replaceable slots and the font families it names.

hostApi.description: The host API range this plugin works with (`^1.0`).

messages.description: The package directory holding `<locale>.json` ICU catalogues.

original.description:
The file on this machine (plan 6A Decision 5: the model's stored path), `null` when it
is missing.

Font bytes for captions (plan 6A Decision 3): the server's font cache, read-only, then the
project's font asset files by SHA-256.

SMPTE ST 2086 mastering display colour volume (`mdcv`), in the box's own units:
chromaticities in 0.00002, luminance in 0.0001 cd/m².

oneOf.description: BT.2020 non-constant luminance.
RGB (GBR) coded directly.

MediaCapabilities.description:
What `media.capabilities` v2 answers: per codec, profile and bit depth what this machine
decodes and encodes and through which backend (with guidance for every gap), the audio
codecs, the encoders that passed their test clip, the GPU a render would use and the worker.

MediaCapabilitiesEvent.description:
`media.capabilities` (`kv` 1): once per server run, what the media worker can decode,
encode and draw on.

duration.description: Seconds: the longest interpreted track after edit lists.

MergeReport.description:
The answer of [`Store::merge`](crate::Store::merge): merge group `merge_id`'s records on
the target, in order (or planned and rolled back, `dry_run`); `merged`: the source txIds
they copy; `skipped`: the candidates that conflict and were left on the source (with
`skipConflicting`; they are offered again by the next merge); `excluded`: source records
never offered (`DROPPED`, `UNDOES_TARGET_RECORDS`); `not_included`: the origin roots of the
candidates the merge's `include` and `sourceUpTo` left on the source, oldest first (plan 5E
Decision 6; omitted when empty); `source_state`: the source branch's state after
the merge; `origins`: `merged` with the records their `origin` chains lead to (a copy of a
copy), first seen first (7A Decision 27). A retry of a committed merge answers from the
log: its records and their origins, `skipped`, `excluded` and `not_included` empty,
`dry_run` false.
Nothing left to merge is an empty answer, not an error.

placements.description:
As [`HistoryResult::placements`], each with its copy's txId, plus the `conflict`
placements of skipped candidates (a retry answers with the copies' stored ones only, as
its `skipped` is empty).

purpose.description: A message key in the `en` catalogue.

NestedPlan.description:
The nested timeline of a group layer, the time evaluated on it (`sourceIn + local`) and

every such request answers `SECRET_MISSING {name}` (injection is 8G's).

The response's head; the body (at most 64 MiB) stays with the host and is read by
`net.read` through `handle` until the job ends (Decision 11).

eof.description: Whether the page reaches the end of the body.

OriginalFile.description:
A file a worker opens, with what it looked like when the manifest was written.

`path` may be absolute anywhere on the machine (the model stores the path the user gave:
plan 6A Decision 5) and the directories above the file may be links: **by design** only the
file itself is opened no-follow and checked against these facts. The manifest is the host's,
written from the project's own model, never from anything a worker or a client sent in the
job; `--replay` of a directory that is not the caller's own is the exception, and confines
originals to the directory (`--originals-anywhere` lifts that). The worker
opens it through `fin-library`'s no-follow opener, which refuses it once its size, mtime or
file id changed (`ORIGINALS_MISSING {reason: changed}`); `mtimeNs` and `fileId` are
encoded as `fin-library`'s `Expect` encodes them (a decimal string; standard base64).

PairRoute.description: How a device reached the server (`ROUTE_KINDS`): a kind, never an address.

PanSegment.description: Pan over `[from, to)` (−1 left … 1 right; the mixer clamps), read like [`GainSegment`].

PanicThread.description: The thread that panicked (the plan's `thread: Name`, as a closed enum).

ParamSet.description: `param.set`: sets `path` of `item` to `value`; no `value` resets it to its default.

ParamSpec.description:
One parameter: its path in its scope, type, whether keyframes may animate it, default, unit
and fix text (`{min}`, `{max}`, `{unit}` and `{path}` are filled in errors).

ParamType.description:
A parameter's value type. Times and rationals are canonical rational text (`"1/2"`),
colours `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa` (lowercase), enums their names; a size is whole pixels as
a `vec2`; an asset reference is `{"asset": id}` of one of `kinds`. Ranges are inclusive.

ParamValue.description:
A parameter value: finite numbers round-trip bit for bit through stored JSON (serde_json's
`float_roundtrip`). Times, rationals, colours (`#rrggbb[aa]`) and enum values are text; an
asset reference is `{"asset": id}`, so every id a value carries is found without the
registry (plan 4C Decision 24).

PendingCompaction.description: One manifest as status shows it.

graceEndsMs.description: Unix ms (this machine's clock, informational) when the grace period ends, once it runs.

state.description:
`arriving` (its packs or snapshot are not all here yet), `grace`, `waiting`,
`abandoned` or `unreadable`.

Permission.description:
One permission, tagged by `perm`. The set is closed: an unknown `perm` or field fails the
parse (a unit permission with any other field too, which serde's tagged enums allow).

PermissionDiff.description: What an update changes in a plugin's grants. Order inside lists never matters.

added.description: Permissions whose key the old set did not have.

removed.description: Keys the new set no longer has.

riskUp.description: The overall risk rose, or a kept permission's risk rose through a combination.

widened.description: Permissions of one key where the new one grants more.

oneOf.description: 8-bit 4:2:0, Y plane then interleaved UV.
10-bit 4:2:0 in 16-bit words (high bits), Y then interleaved UV.
8-bit 4:2:0, three planes.
10-bit 4:2:0, three planes of 16-bit words (low bits).
8-bit 4:2:2, three planes.
10-bit 4:2:2, three planes of 16-bit words (low bits).
8-bit 4:4:4, three planes.
10-bit 4:4:4, three planes of 16-bit words (low bits).

Placeholder.description:
A cloud placeholder (Decision 12): catalogued from metadata only, never opened unless the
library has `hydrate`.

oneOf.description: macOS `SF_DATALESS`, on a file or a directory.
A legacy iCloud `.<name>.icloud` stub, standing for `<name>`.
A Nextcloud `<name>.nextcloud` virtual file, standing for `<name>`.
An ownCloud `<name>.owncloud` virtual file, standing for `<name>`.
Windows `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_OPEN`.
Windows `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS`.
Windows `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_OFFLINE`.
Windows `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_UNPINNED`: online-only even with the other bits clear.

Placement.description:
The placement of one item an undo, redo or copy put back (module docs): which op of which
record, the item, the outcome, and for a relocation where it landed and why.

PlacementOutcome.description: The placement outcome of one restored item.

PlanCrop.description:
A layer's crop, resolved at the plan's time: fractions of the item's size cut from each
side, each in `[0, 1]`, every field present.

displayName.description: The id's name until manifests carry a display name.

publisher.description: The manifest's publisher name (shown to people, never journaled).

PlanSample.description:
The BLAKE3 of a frame plan at one time (plan 6A Decision 4): lowercase hex of the plan's
compact JSON, as `fin-core`'s eval corpus hashes it.

PlanTransform.description:
A layer's transform, resolved at the plan's time: every field is present (the model's
`Transform` leaves defaults out).

**The base box** (sub-project 6 spec §5.1, owner question 4: "contain"): a source's display
size (after its rotation and pixel aspect) fitted inside the timeline frame and centred.
The item is that box with item-normalised coordinates 0…1; its `anchor` point is placed at
the frame centre plus `position`, and the item is scaled by `scale` and rotated `rotation`
degrees clockwise about it. The defaults leave the base box where it is. `crop` cuts
fractions of the base box from each side without moving the rest.

anyOf.description: An asset reference (a `lut` effect's asset, an image slot), `{"asset": id}` as stored.

PlanValue.description: A resolved value (plan 4C Decision 12): colours are sRGB `[r, g, b, a]` in 0…1.

PlanWarning.description:
A warning shown with the plan: `thirdPartyCode {confined}`, `yanked`, `advisory` (from the
registry), `lookalikeId {similar}`, `copyleft {spdx}`, `licenceUnknown {spdx}`,
`registryStale {days}`.

risk.description: Within the whole set (combinations count, spec §4.3).

Platform.description: The shipped OS and architecture pairs (the triples of `deny.toml`), in Node's spelling.

PluginCommand.description: `plugin.command`: one run of a plugin command (`plugin.command.run`).

args.description: Training only: the arguments as validated.

ops.description: Op kind → count of the ops it returned (`OP_KINDS`).

command.description: The command's name in its manifest.

name.description: The registry name, `plugin:<id>/<command>` (the name 7B's command rules match).

plugin.description: `<id>@<version>` of the enabled plugin that serves it.

timeoutS.description: Its timeout in seconds (the manifest's, 10 when absent, at most 60).

title.description: A message key in the plugin's `en` catalogue.

writes.description: Whether it returns a transaction (running it needs `project.write`).

PluginCommandList.description:
`plugin.commands`: `digest` is the BLAKE3 of the canonical JSON of `commands`, so a client
caches the list per server and digest.

PluginCommandOutcome.description:
How a plugin command ended (spec §11; `failed`: the process crashed, broke the protocol or
the host failed, a deviation: the spec's list has no outcome for it).

oneOf.description: Its transaction was committed as is (or, with `dryRun`, validated).
Committed after a rebase.
Refused by a check (permission, reach, a disabled plugin).

Its arguments or its returned ops were invalid (`PLUGIN_COMMAND_ARGS`,
`PLUGIN_TX_INVALID`).
It returned data, not a transaction.

branch.description: A branch name, id or `name#id`; `main` when absent.

dryRun.description: Validate the returned transaction against the snapshot the plugin saw; commit nothing.

data.description: A data command's value as the plugin returned it.

dryRun.description: A dry run: nothing was committed.

rev.description: The committed revision; for a dry run or a conflict, the revision the plugin saw.

grants.description:
The permissions granted to this plugin (the job's rights are the invoker's
intersected with these, checked by the host on every call).

hostApi.description: The host API the running host implements.

locale.description: The invoker's locale (a BCP 47 tag) for plugin-facing text.

The caller's `pluginData` directory, only when `fs pluginData` is granted (spec §5.1):
`plugins/data/@pub/name/<projectId|_>/` for uniform `person`/`system` rights, else
`plugins/authdata/@pub/name/<projectId|_>/<authorityKey>/`.

The egress broker's counts for one plugin in a `plugin.stats` window (Task 8's counters,
differenced per window). Refusals by reason; no origin, URL or body.

denied.description: `EGRESS_DENIED`: an origin it was not granted.

PluginExit.description: `plugin.exit`: a plugin process ended (built from the same exit as its `worker.exit`).

PluginInfo.description: Everything a registry signs about one plugin.

advisories.description: In-scope advisories that apply to at least one listed version.

versions.description: Every version, yanked ones included, oldest first.

PluginInput.description: A code plugin's process (sp8 §16.1, plan 7C Decisions 9 and 21).

callDir.description: The call's or job's directory: `in/` is read-only, `out/` writable.

gpu.description: GPU device nodes; empty without the `gpu` grant. Never `/dev/dri/card*`.

memoryBytes.description: The manifest's declared memory need (default 2 GiB, at most 16 GiB; sp8 §3.3).

models.description: The model files the manifest names.

pluginData.description: The per-project plugin data directory, when the manifest is granted `fs pluginData`.

runtime.description: The runtime: finisherd's Node or the Electron framework, for `node` plugins.

oneOf.description: Data only, validated in Rust by the batch that consumes it.
OS processes under the `plugin` sandbox profile (8B).

PluginKindName.description: `content` or `code`; `unknown` when the call failed before a manifest was read.

PluginLifecycle.description:
`plugin.lifecycle`: one plugin call (plan, install, update, downgrade, remove, enable,
disable, revoke).

bytesLog2.description: The package's unpacked bytes as a log₂ bucket ([`log2_bucket`]).

permissionsAdded.description:
Permissions added or widened against the installed version (all of them for a first
install), capped at 255.

PluginMethodStats.description: One method family's calls in a `plugin.stats` window.

bytesInLog2.description: Params bytes over the window, as a log₂ bucket.

bytesOutLog2.description: Reply bytes over the window, as a log₂ bucket.

oneOf.description: Refused by a check (validation, a hash, TUF, a permission): `code` says which.
Failed for another reason (I/O, internal).

PluginRef.description:
A plugin as the journal names it: a bundled plugin by its table name, any other by the
journal's keyed hash of its id.

A sub-project 5 scope a plugin job may hold, each from one permission (spec §3.7):
`project:read` → `project.read`; `project:write` → `project.write` (only the `tx.commit` of
the command's returned transaction); `media:read` → `library.read` (and asset reads);
`jobs:submit` → `jobs.submit` (the plugin's own kinds only, 8C).

PluginStats.description:
`plugin.stats`: one plugin's host traffic over one window (a minute), sent when the
plugin did anything in it.

families.description: Per method family (`PLUGIN_METHOD_FAMILIES`), each at most once.

logDropped.description: `log` calls dropped by the rate limit.

stderrDropped.description: stderr lines dropped by the byte limit.

oneOf.description: BT.601 625-line (BT.470 B/G; PAL).

`settings.json` `privacy` (Decision 8). Absent keys fall through to the defaults; unknown
keys are ignored.

rotation, colour, HDR, VFR, edit lists. In the `asset.probe` answer only: an

from it); the worker works from the job directory.

fingerprint make the job's identity (`dedupe`): another decoder set probes again.

the capability probe). Absent: a keyframe every 0.25 s.

[`proxy_key`] of the fields above: where the host commits the entry. The worker writes
`out/<key>/` and fails `PLAN_MISMATCH {reason: cacheKey}` when the decoder it opened
gives another key.

projectId.description:
The project that asked (host only: `prepare` writes the manifest from its branch head,
`onSucceeded` commits the entry for it).

ProxyResult.description: What `media.proxy` v1 answers for its item (the fingerprint).

backend.description: The encoder's backend (`svt-av1`, `videotoolbox`, `mf-hw`, …) and its vendor class.

bytes.description: The entry's bytes (its files, `meta.json` not included).

frames.description: Proxy frames: the original's presented frames.

oneOf.description: Scrub and remote clients: fits 960 × 540.
The default preview: fits 1920 × 1080.

ProxyTierStatus.description: One tier of `media.proxy.status`: its entry when the cache holds one, the job making it.

state.description:
`ready` (in the cache), `making` (a job runs), `failed` (the last job failed) or
`none`.

oneOf.description: Everything: every file, every blob, the key and `state.json`.
The entries of one project (`ctx.project`; a project id, lower-cased).
The entries with `ts` before this (ms since the epoch).

Purpose.description: A purpose events are recorded for.

QuarantineSummary.description: Records set aside now (`current` quarantine rows).

oneOf.description: Video range: Y 16–235, chroma 16–240 (8-bit).

Rational.description: Exact rational seconds in canonical form: "n/d" in lowest terms with d > 1, or "n" when d is 1; no leading zeros, no "+", no "-0". The pattern checks the shape; lowest terms is checked by the parser.

RawRel.description: Raw components below a library root, outermost first (empty for the root): base64 of each name's bytes (Unix bytes; Windows UTF-16 as WTF-8).

Reach.description: Which projects or libraries a job reaches: `"all"` or a list of ids.

ReachAll.description: `"all"`: every project (or library) of this server.

ReadOnlyReason.description:
Why the project is read-only (spec §3.7). Import sets `ChainFork`, `ConflictCopy`,
`NewerFormat` and `ImportError`; the lease sets `LeaseHeld`, `LeaseLost` and
`CatchingUp` (`Store::read_only` combines them).

Not in the spec's table (Task 20 adds them):
- `ImportError`: a record on the resolved chain cannot be applied
  ([`ImportReport::error`]). Writing past it would build a line that servers able to
  replay it see as a fork, so commits and export wait until a later pass no longer
  reports it.
- `CatchingUp`: the lease was just acquired, and no import pass at the new epoch has yet
  resolved every branch with nothing waiting (after waiting out the directory-cache
  window when another server wrote before). Until then a commit or an export could extend
  a line the folder has already moved past (plan Task 11, ordering rule).

Precedence, highest first: `ChainFork`, `ConflictCopy`, `NewerFormat`, `ImportError`
(the folder's content: a person or an update must act, whoever holds the lease), then
`LeaseLost`, `LeaseHeld`, `CatchingUp` (the lease: resolved by waiting or a takeover).

corruptCopy.description:
Where the old database was kept (`project.fdb.corrupt-<ts>`, or
`project.fdb.replaced-<ts>` after a manual rebuild).

genesisMismatch.description:
The project file's genesis does not describe the old database's rev 0 (that rev 0
was used).

importError.description: Why the import stopped early (it stopped where any open would).

keptForRecovery.description:
Kept copies whose salvage could not read everything and that are not acknowledged:
never pruned (`Store::acknowledge_salvage`).

missingFromFolder.description: Of those, exported records the folder no longer yields (`MISSING_FROM_FOLDER`).

problem.description: What made the old database count as damaged (`corrupt`).

rebuiltThrough.description: The head of `main` in the new database.

salvageComplete.description: Everything in the old databases could be read.

salvaged.description:
Rows salvaged into quarantine: records the new database lacks (`SALVAGED`,
`MISSING_FROM_FOLDER`) and the old databases' own quarantine rows.

seededFromSnapshot.description: The seq of the folder snapshot the rebuild was seeded from.

verify.description: The checks of the new database that need no replay.

RecipeUsage.description: One recipe's share of the cache.

RecordKind.description:
What a record does (spec §4.2). Sub-project 4A writes only edits; 4B adds the rest up to
`branchSet`; 5E adds `drop` (durable rejections, sub-project 5 spec §8.3).

RecoverReport.description:
[`Store::recover`](crate::Store::recover)'s answer: the groups as found (before `create`),
the branches made and every record written (`branch` records on the parents, the copies,
checkpoints, `branchSet` records), in order, for publishing; `imported`: quarantine rows
`import_dir` added or made current again, and `skipped_files` the files it did not read;
`dismissed`: rows `dismiss` set aside from listing and counting; `manual`: the procedure
for a read-only state recovery cannot lift by itself (`CHAIN_FORK`, `CONFLICT_COPY`).

rootsAdded.description: Roots newly trusted by this refresh.

staleDays.description: Whole days the metadata is past its earliest expiry, when it is.

RegistryProblem.description:
A registry that could not be opened (its config or trusted set is damaged); the others
are still listed.

RegistryRefresh.description: `registry.refresh`: one refresh of a registry's trusted metadata.

byHuman.description: A human principal asked for it (agents' and `system`'s refreshes install nothing).

staleDays.description: Days the registry's metadata is past its expiry (relaxed freshness), when it is.

targetsLog2.description: Targets listed after the refresh, as a log₂ bucket.

RegistryStatus.description: One added registry (spec §5.1: `registry.json` and the trusted set).

advisories.description: Advisories in scope of the trusted set.

kind.description: `local`: a folder (a git registry is a folder the user pulls).

lastRefreshAt.description: Seconds since the epoch of the last successful refresh, `None` before the first.

maxStaleDays.description: `maxStaleDays` from the signed root (default 7, at most 90).

plugins.description: Plugins listed (with at least one version), yanked-only ones included.

rootSha256.description: The root this registry is trusted through (also the name of its trust directory).

staleDays.description: Whole days past the trusted metadata's earliest expiry, `None` while fresh.

RenderManifest.description:
`in/manifest.json` (spec §4.2): built by `fin-node` from the snapshot's asset table,
never by the worker.

assets.description: Every asset the snapshot references, once.

RenderPhase.description: A stage of a render, for [`RenderStats`].

oneOf.description: No emitter before sub-project 6B (export).

RenderStats.description:
`render.stats` (`kv` 1): per-minute histograms of render stages in micros, one entry per
phase and backend. `backend` is the decode backend for `decode` and the GPU API for
`composite` and `readback`. A worker sends what it measured since its last job ended, so
several entries may share a window (`histogram.start`): readers add them.

ResolutionBucket.description:
A frame size as a bucket: the smallest standard size the frame fits within, by pixel count
(so a portrait clip buckets as its landscape twin): `sd` ≤ 960×540, `hd720` ≤ 1280×720,
`hd1080` ≤ 2048×1080, `qhd` ≤ 2560×1440, `uhd4k` ≤ 4096×2160, `uhd8k` above.

Retry.description: How the engine may retry after a worker `error` (Decision 31).

oneOf.description: Deterministic: no retry (the default).
Transient (I/O, an offline root): retry with backoff.
Retry once, at once, on a fresh process (`GPU_DEVICE_LOST`).

ReviewEntry.description:
One entry of a review plan: a source record (`tx_id` on `branch` at `seq`) and its origin
root (`origin`, what decisions and `include` name), its kind, record author, number of
intent ops and commit time (unix ms), and what the merge does with it. `reason`: the
conflict or exclusion reason (absent for `willMerge` and `alreadyPresent`); `blame`: the
record a conflict is blamed on, when there is one. `actor`: the agent actor the server
knows for the record (sub-project 7A's tracker), never set by the planner.

ReviewHead.description:
A branch head as a review plan saw it: the branch id, its head seq and the `txHash` of the
record there (absent at a root's start), so a rewind to the same seq is told apart (plan 5E
Decision 9).

ReviewItemKind.description: What the verdict is about (`none` for the outcome tracker's entries).

ReviewPlan.description:
[`Store::review_plan`](crate::Store::review_plan)'s answer (plan 5E Decision 7): what a
merge of `source` into `target` would do at these heads, one entry per candidate and per
source record the target already holds, oldest first; `conflicts`: the candidates that
conflict (as a `skipConflicting` merge would skip them). At most
[`REVIEW_PLAN_MAX`](crate::REVIEW_PLAN_MAX) entries and conflicts, the oldest:
`truncated` when there were more.

accepted.description: Counts of the transactions accepted and rejected by the decision.

openS.description: Seconds since the item opened (or since the transaction, for the tracker's entries).

reason.description: Training only: the reason the person gave.

RightsBranch.description:
An agent session's branch reach (sub-project 7 §5.1): its root branch and, with `subtree`,
the branches beneath it (less its live children's).

RightsPrincipal.description: The invoking principal (sub-project 5's `{kind, id}`; the job's owner).

RiskName.description: The overall risk shown to people (spec §4.3); `unknown` as for [`PluginKindName`].

Role.description: Which side of a transition a layer is.

oneOf.description: The outgoing item (A).
The incoming item (B).

RootState.description:
A root's state (Decision 17): `online` carries the identity measured now (its key may
differ from the stored one when the change was confirmed harmless); every other state
puts the library offline with its catalog intact (Decision 18).

Rotation.description: Clockwise display rotation in degrees, from the track matrix.

Runtime.description: How a code plugin runs (spec §3.2). `python` and `wasm` are after v1.

oneOf.description: One executable per platform, by package path; its keys are the manifest's `platforms`.
One bundled `.mjs` file run by finisherd's own Node, which must satisfy `node`.

SampleEntry.description:
One top-level entry of a root, kept to confirm a volume change (Decision 17). No name:
entries are matched by file id, size and mtime.

Sandbox.description: The worker sandbox in force (spec §3.5): `none` in 6A.

SandboxMechanism.description: What a profile gets on this host.

oneOf.description: Applied, with what (`landlock abi 8`).
Runs unconfined, with warnings (F2).
The start is refused: the host lacks `need`.

SandboxNamespaces.description:
Whether `fin-sandbox-exec` can hide Unix sockets from `agent` and `hook` processes in a user
and mount namespace on this host (plan 7C Decision 26). Only the launcher binary can tell
(an AppArmor profile attaches to it by path), so `finisherd` asks it: `--probe`.

Not Linux.

SandboxOs.description: The operating system a sandbox applies on.

SandboxStatus.description: Every profile's status on this host (`sandboxStatus()` in fin-node).

ScanBatch.description: One batch file of a scan (Decision 26): up to 4,096 entries, in `seq` order per job.

ScanEntry.description:
One entry of a directory listing, as a scan reports it (Decision 25 keys rows by
`(dir, name)` on raw bytes).

- `name`: the raw component the entry is opened by; for a Nextcloud, ownCloud or iCloud
  stub it is the name the stub **stands for** (`placeholder` says which stub), so the row
  survives hydration; a stub whose real file is also listed is `excluded` with

- `name_nfc`, `name_lossy`: the NFC display name ([`crate::names`]); `rel_key`: the
  lookup key, `/`-joined and case-folded on case-insensitive roots. Neither is unique.
- `dev`, `file_id`: rename hints only (`dev:fileId`, Decision 22); `None` where the OS or
  server gives none.
- `mount_root`: the entry is the root of a nested mount; `automount`: an automount point,
  never descended (`excluded: AUTOMOUNT`).
- `excluded`: the exclusion code ([`crate::exclude::code`]) or `None`.

ScanTrigger.description:
What started a scan: `add` (the first scan), `schedule` (the poll cadence or the full-scan
schedule), `demand` (someone asked, a freshness pass, a file found changed), `watch` (a local
root's watcher), `mount` (the root came back online).

SchemaError.description: Why a schema is outside the subset: `at` is a JSON pointer into the schema.

Scope.description:
Where a parameter lives. An effect's paths are `<kind>.<param>`; on an item they are
addressed as `effects.<fx>.<param>`.

Scrubbed.description: Finisher-authored text with paths, the home, data and temp directories, the user name and the host name replaced by placeholders.

The plugin receives the secret's value.

SelfSandbox.description: A requested self-sandbox: a profile name and its arguments.

SessionStart.description:
The process run began (the journal opened with a purpose on, or one turned on). Platform
facts only (Decision 5): no host, user, IP, serial or hardware model.

memGiB.description: Memory rounded to a power-of-two GiB.

SessionUnclean.description: A start found the previous run still open in `state.json`.

Shape.description:
A fade or crossfade side over a segment: `p` is its progress at the segment's ends (0 → 1
across the whole fade). Its amplitude factor is `curve(p)` for `fadeIn`/`crossIn` and
`curve(1 − p)` for `fadeOut`/`crossOut` (`linear`: `x`; `equalPower`: `sqrt(x)`-shaped, as
the mixer defines it).

Shift.description:
Items on `track` at or after `from` moved by `by` (ripple), recorded by op `op` of the
transaction.

SignIn.description: The kind of sign-in a CLI harness reports (CLI harnesses only).

versions.description: A semver range of affected versions.

A file `import_dir` did not read: its path and why (`not a segment: …`, `another
project`, `too large: …`, `unreadable: …`).

SlideSides.description: The neighbours an internal `item.slide` trims; a side without one trims nothing there.

SlotSpec.description: One replaceable slot of a template: its id and value kind (as the template declares it).

Which program emitted an entry. The server sets it from the connection's principal (5A
Decision 27: `local` and `agent` → `fin`, `mcp` → `mcp`, `console` → `console`, `device` →
`ui`), never from the payload. `console`, a person at the server, sends no events of its
own; `mcp`, the MCP adapter (D16), sends the kinds `fin` does.

SourceRef.description: An asset and the time to read from it, in seconds.

Stacks.description: An author's undo and redo stacks on a branch, bottom first (the top is the last entry).

StatusWarning.description:
One status warning (`StatusWarning` in the schema). The store's carry a code and a message; the server's font warnings
(fin-node, 4C Decision 34) also `details` and a `fix`.

StorageKind.description: The project folder's storage kind: `local`, `network` or `sync:<provider>`.

Stroke.description: An outline around the glyphs. A stroke equal to the default (width 0) is no stroke.

StyleAdd.description: `style.add`: a project style named `name`, from `from`, with `set` applied.

StyleSet.description:
`style.set`: sets `path` of `style` to `value`; no `value` resets it to the default
style's (or removes an optional part).

SupportClass.description: How a codec direction is served: hardware, software, or not at all.

TargetCustom.description:
A package target's signed custom metadata (`custom` in its publisher's delegated role): one
type for the editor that signs it, the TUF client that reads it and the plan that checks it.

TestCallParams.description: `test.call`: one host call; returns the reply.

TestCheckpointParams.description:
`test.checkpoint` (resumable): a checkpoint per step; crashes on attempt 1 at
`crashAt`.

TestCrashHow.description:
How `test.crash` dies: `abort`, `SIGSEGV`/an access violation, `SIGBUS`/
`EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR`, Windows `__fastfail`, `exit(3)`, or by allocating until its
group's memory limit kills it (`oom`; it aborts past 2 GiB).

TestCrashParams.description:
`test.crash` (batch): `begin`/`item` per item; crashes inside a poison item (before
its `begin` with `between`), or inside the second item of any run of two or more with
`crashOnSecond`.

TestDetach.description: `test.spawn`: the grandchild stays in the group or leaves it with `setsid`.

TestEchoParams.description: `test.echo`: returns `value`, plus what `report` asks about the process.

TestEchoReport.description: What `test.echo` reports about its own process.

TestFailParams.description:
`test.fail`: answers `error {code, retry}` on every attempt up to `failUntil` (every
attempt without it), then succeeds with the attempt number.

hash.description: FNV-1a 64 of the content after the run, as hex.

TestFilesParams.description:
`test.files`: writes a pattern into every `write` file, reads every `read` file, and
leaves a file in each `write` directory; fails (`retry: backoff`) on attempt
`failOnAttempt`.

TestGarbageParams.description: `test.garbage`: commits the protocol violation `what`, then waits to be killed.

TestHangParams.description: `test.hang`: stops `alive`, stops reading stdin (EOF unseen, the pipe fills) and blocks.

TestHelperParams.description: `test.helper`: the job of a test helper (`helper` picks its behaviour).

TestOomParams.description:
`test.oom`: allocates and touches `mib` MiB, maps `mapFile` (if given) read-only and
reads every page of it, writes `1` to `readyFile` (if given), then holds.

holdMs.description: Hold the memory this long before answering.

mapFile.description: A file (mapped name, or under the job directory) to map: file-backed pages.

readyFile.description: A file to write once the memory is held.

TestPluginMinorParams.description:
`test.pluginMinor` (family `testplugin`): `hello` with minor 1 and no envelope, then a
message of an unknown type with an `id`. `key` is its warm key.

TestProgressFloodParams.description:
`test.progressFlood`: `n` progress messages as fast as it can; with `stderrBytes`, `n`
stderr lines of that many bytes (`flood <i> ` then padding) instead.

TestSpawnParams.description:
`test.spawn` (breaks the no-process rule on purpose): double-forks a sleeping
grandchild, writes the pids to the mapped file `out`, then sleeps.

grandchildMs.description: How long the grandchild sleeps (default 600 s).

TestSpawnPids.description: What `test.spawn` writes to its `out` file (JSON, then zero padding).

TestStallParams.description: `test.stall`: keeps `alive`, never reports progress, ends at cancel.

TestWarmParams.description: `test.warm` (warm): returns `value` with the pid and how many jobs the process served.

holdFile.description: A job-directory file kept open past `ready` (breaks the warm contract on purpose).

probe.description:
Paths the worker tries to read (plan 7C Task 12): each answered with the errno of
the attempt, `null` when it read. A path starting with `!` is renamed instead (to
`<path>.moved`, and back when it worked): what replacing it with a link would need.

probes.description: One errno (or `null`) per `probe` path, in order.

TextLayout.description:
A measured layout, all lengths in 1/64 px. `width` is the widest line's ink, `height` the
lines' total advance. `overflow` is set when a line's ink box reaches outside
`0..max_width` (on either side) or there are more lines than `max_lines`. `missing` lists the code points no face maps (ascending);
`faces` the sha256s whose glyphs the layout uses, in request order.

TextStyle.description: The style a text is measured with.

letterSpacing.description:
Extra advance between shaping clusters (a base with its combining marks, or a
ligature), in em (a multiple of `size`; may be negative); none after a line's last.

lineHeight.description: Line advance as a multiple of `size` (e.g. 1.2).

ToneMapped.description: How an HDR source was brought to SDR (Decision 9).

oneOf.description: By the OS (`VTPixelTransferSession`, macOS).
By the compositor's ingest shader (`fin_media::colour::tonemap`).

TrainingState.description:
Training's state: `undecided` until a person answers (the onboarding question). It
records no content, exactly like `off`.

oneOf.description: BT.709 (also BT.601 and BT.2020 SDR, whose curves are the same).
SMPTE ST 2084.
ARIB STD-B67.

Transition.description: A transition at the cut between two touching items of one track, centred on the cut.

between.description: The outgoing item, then the incoming one.

TransitionKind.description:
How a transition mixes its two items (sub-project 6 spec §4.3): both mix by
`curve(progress)`; they differ in the space they mix in.

oneOf.description: Mixes display-encoded (BT.1886) values.
Mixes linear light.

TransitionSet.description:
`transition.set`: the transition at the cut between `between[0]` (outgoing) and
`between[1]` (incoming), touching items of `track`, centred on the cut. `id` is a `$name`
placeholder to create one, or the literal id of the one to update (a literal id naming no
transition restores it: internal only).

TransitionState.description:
A layer inside a transition window `[cut − d/2, cut + d/2)`: `progress` runs 0 → 1 over it.

**Looks** (sub-project 6 spec §4.3, §5.1): the outgoing layer is drawn as it is; the incoming
one is drawn over it and mixed with what is below by `curve(progress)` (`linear`: the
progress; `equalPower`: its square root). `crossfade` mixes display-encoded values,
`dissolve` linear light.

TrimMode.description:
How a trim treats the rest of the track: `ripple` moves every later item by the change;
`roll` moves the cut between the item and the neighbour touching that edge (both change,
nothing else moves; `NOT_ADJACENT` without one); `overwrite` moves the edge itself, carving
whatever it extends over and leaving a gap when it shrinks; `strict` (internal: the inverse
of carving edits) moves the edge only, and an overlap it would make is `CLIP_OVERLAP` in
every apply mode.

TrustedVersions.description: The versions of the trusted metadata roles; a role not yet fetched has none.

TurnPurpose.description: Why a model call was made, when it is not the conversation's next step (7B Decision 24).

oneOf.description: The built-in loop's summary call, whose reply replaces the runs before the current one.

argsHash.description:
What produced the tx, for a client that sends an idempotency key as `txId`:
`blake3:<64 hex>` of the command input (op kinds and canonical args, before they were
resolved against a snapshot). A retry rebuilds `ops` against a newer head (positions
move; the stored tx is rebased), so `ops` cannot tell a retry from another command;
this can. The store refuses a `txId` it holds with another `argsHash`
(`IDEM_KEY_REUSED`). Stored with the record, so every server that imported it checks.

TxIntent.description:
An edit intent (content `txIntent`): the transactions as committed (an edit's one tx, or a
history call's records, at most [`MAX_INTENT_TXS`]), or the request's normalised tx on
failure.

TxSetAside.description: `tx.get` for a transaction that is not (or no longer) on its branch.

UnconfinedReason.description: Why a profile runs unconfined (F2: both run, with persistent warnings).

oneOf.description:
The OS mechanism is off on this host (Linux: `landlock` left out of `lsm=`, or a
container's seccomp profile refusing the Landlock calls).
The profile's escape suite has not yet passed on this OS (`fin_sandbox::READY`).

source.description:
The record whose stored `inverse` an undo uses: the unit's records, or the redo
record that recreated it (Decision 23).

UnitSource.description: Where an undo takes a unit's inverse from ([`UnitEntry::source`]).

oneOf.description: The unit's own records.
The redo record `tx_id`, which recreated an undone unit.

Unmeasured.description: Why a caption has no layout, and the font keys concerned.

ValidationReport.description: `validateManifest`: the manifest when valid, else every violation.

The codec plugin (spec §6.5).

Verdict.description: What was decided or became of the work.

VerdictVia.description: How the outcome came about; absent for a person's decision on an item.

target.description: The target name, its signed length and SHA-256.

Via.description:
The plugin command a transaction came from: `plugin` is `<id>@<version>`. Only the host's
plugin host (`apps/finisherd/src/plugins/host/commands.ts`) writes it; any other `via` is
stripped. fin-core never validates it: to everything here it is unchecked data.

oneOf.description: Anything else; the sample entry's four-character code is in `VideoTrackInfo.fourcc`.

display.description: `coded` after the pixel aspect and the rotation ([`display_size`]).

icc.description: An ICC profile was given instead of code points (`colr` `prof`/`rICC`).

nominalRate.description: Frames per second of the most common frame duration.

pixelAspect.description: Horizontal over vertical spacing (`pasp`); 1 when absent.

Warning.description: A warning `{code, details}`, e.g. `REGISTRY_STALE {days, maxStaleDays, role}`.

Weights.description: The model's weights class, from the catalogue at the time (§12.7).

Widening.description: One permission an update widens: the same `perm`, granting more.

WordBox.description:
One word's ink box on its line (see [`LineBox`]; visual order is given by `x`). A word
that draws nothing has a zero-width box at its pen position.

WordPlan.description:
One word: item-relative times clamped to the item, and whether it is spoken at the plan's
time (`start ≤ local < end`).

`worker.exit` (`kv` 2: `plugin` is a [`PluginRef`], Decision 22 of sp8b; `kv` 1 had a

WorkerSandbox.description: The OS confinement the worker applied to itself (spec §3.5.1).

oneOf.description: 7C's Linux Landlock `worker` profile (6B-1 Task 18).
7C's full `worker` profile on every OS (6G).
One job: its `in/` (read), its `out/` (write) and the manifest's source files.

sources.description: The manifest's sources, per file where the OS allows it (read-only).

oneOf.description:
A warm worker: its own directory (each job it serves is created under
`<workerDir>/jobs/<jobId>/`, Decision 19), never the jobs root, and one project's
sources and library roots (owner decision 2026-11-08: one warm worker per project).

libraryRoots.description: The project's `sources/` and the library roots it references (read-only).

WriteGuard.description:
The branches a write may change, by branch id (`br<n>`, `main`). The default guards
nothing.

allowBranches.description:
When set, the only branches a write may change (`BRANCH_NOT_ALLOWED` otherwise). Absent
means no allow-list; `null` is refused, so a sender's bug cannot open the guard.

credential.description:
The credential the write is made for (`agent:<id>`, `mcp:<id>`), refused once it has
been ended ([`end_credential`]); absent for `local` and `console`. `null` is refused.
